mainTopic: Paying the difference when הקדש is sold for the wrong price (אונאה, ביטול מקח, appraisals), and the closing משנה of כיצד מערימין on 'in place of' and unfit animals
overview: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about someone who redeemed הקדש for less than it was worth: is the difference owed by Torah law or only by rabbinic law? A teaching in רבי יוחנן's name about אונאה and ביטול מקח seems to clash with his view. רבי ירמיה applies that teaching to regular land and רבי יונה applies it to הקדש. The גמרא first answers by switching the two names, but then shows that the switch works only for רבי יונה's version. רבי ירמיה says that in his version no switch is needed. The גמרא then explains the gap between רבי יונה and רבי ירמיה through שמואל's rule about redeeming הקדש for a פרוטה: both accept the rule, but they disagree about whether it applies only after the fact (דיעבד) or even from the start (לכתחילה). It also offers another answer: never switch the names, and read the משנה of אלו דברים the way רב חסדא does. עולא then rules that an appraisal of הקדש by three people is final, because the appraisal is only rabbinic. The פרק ends with a new משנה about saying 'in place of' an offering and about setting aside unfit animals 'for' an offering, and רב shows that this משנה does not follow רבי מאיר or רבי שמעון.

steps.title: A challenge from רבי יוחנן's teaching about אונאה and ביטול מקח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching in רבי יוחנן's name that ביטול מקח does apply. This seems to clash with the earlier view that he only requires paying the difference by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי ירמיה say about regular (non-holy) land, and רבי יונה say about הקדש, both quoting רבי יוחנן: the rules of אונאה do not apply to them, but ביטול מקח does apply to them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking how it explained the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. It quotes a teaching in רבי יוחנן's name that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that for these items a small overcharge (אונאה) does not count, but a big overcharge cancels the sale (ביטול מקח). According to רבי יונה this applies to הקדש, so by Torah law a big gap matters for הקדש. Then how could רבי יוחנן say that paying the difference to הקדש is only rabbinic?

keyTerms.meaning: Regular, non-holy land
Property that belongs to the Temple (holy property)
Overcharging; normally a gap of one-sixth of the price, which must be paid back
Cancelling the sale; this happens when the gap is more than one-sixth
Both of them

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two levels. אונאה is the smaller gap (one-sixth) that is paid back. ביטול מקח is the bigger gap (more than one-sixth) that cancels the whole sale. רבי יוחנן's teaching says these items are free from the first but not from the second.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yirmeya say this regarding non-sacred lands,
and Rabbi Yona said it regarding consecrated property,
and both of them said it in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
They do not have the rules of exploitation (overcharging),
but they do have nullification of the sale!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argument that came just before this passage.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן holds that making up the gap for הקדש, when it is more than one-sixth, is only rabbinic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יונה reports that רבי יוחנן holds ביטול מקח applies to הקדש. So by Torah law a big gap matters for הקדש, which contradicts the 'only rabbinic' position.

steps.title: It is about ביטול מקח, but switch the names
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא keeps the idea that the argument is about ביטול מקח, but switches which view belongs to רבי יוחנן and which to ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, they argue about ביטול מקח, and switch the names around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The argument really is about a gap of more than one-sixth, but we must switch the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the names switched, רבי יוחנן becomes the one who says the gap is owed by Torah law. That fits his teaching that ביטול מקח applies. ריש לקיש now holds the 'only rabbinic' view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really' or 'actually'; the גמרא keeps its original idea
Switch around; swap the names of the two opinions

phrases.english: Actually, it is about nullification of a sale, and reverse the opinions.
phrases.notes: 'Reverse' means swap the names: what we said in רבי יוחנן's name is really ריש לקיש's view, and the other way around.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the names of the opinions (איפוך)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן holds the gap is owed only by rabbinic law, which clashes with his teaching about ביטול מקח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names are switched. רבי יוחנן holds the gap is owed by Torah law, which fits his teaching that ביטול מקח applies.

steps.title: Can we really switch? It works for רבי יונה's version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the switch. It first grants that the switch works for רבי יונה, who says רבי יוחנן applies ביטול מקח to הקדש, and so all the more to land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can you really say to switch them? That works well for the one who said it was about הקדש, and all the more so about land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new challenge against the switch. In this step it only grants the case where the switch works. This sets up the problem that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן applies ביטול מקח even to הקדש (רבי יונה's version), then the switched view fits him: a gap owed to הקדש counts by Torah law. Land would be covered all the more so.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And can you really say?'; this opens a challenge
'That works well', said about one side before showing the side where there is a problem
All the more so

phrases.english: But can you really say to reverse them?
This works well for the one who said it was about consecrated property,
phrases.notes: That is רבי יונה's version of רבי יוחנן's teaching from step 1.

phrases.english: and all the more so about lands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The switch of names (איפוך) from step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The switch only works for one version of רבי יוחנן's teaching. This step shows the version where it works, and the next step shows where it fails.

steps.title: The switch fails for רבי ירמיה's version
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי ירמיה, רבי יוחנן applies ביטול מקח only to land and not to הקדש. So switching the names would contradict רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the one who said it was about land, and that הקדש has no ביטול מקח, how can he switch this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. Under רבי ירמיה's version, the switch does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה says רבי יוחנן applies ביטול מקח only to regular land, so for הקדש a big gap does not matter by Torah law. If we switch the names, רבי יוחנן would say the gap owed to הקדש is Torah law. That goes against his own teaching, so the problem from step 1 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But for the one who says'; this brings the side where there is a problem
How?

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the switch from step 2 does not settle the question. The גמרא will need a different way to explain the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: But for the one who said it was about lands,
phrases.notes: That is רבי ירמיה's version of רבי יוחנן's teaching.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת אֵין לָהֶן בִּיטּוּל מִקָּח,
phrases.english: but consecrated property has no nullification of a sale,
how can he reverse this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge started in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The switch of names (איפוך) from step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי ירמיה, רבי יוחנן holds that הקדש has no ביטול מקח. So רבי יוחנן cannot be the one who says the gap owed to הקדש is a Torah obligation.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: Do Not Switch the Names
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge from step 4: in his version, there is no need to switch the names of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Do not reverse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the problem from step 4 by saying: don't switch the names. Keep רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש exactly as they were first quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The switch was only needed to fit רבי יונה's report that רבי יוחנן applies ביטול מקח to הקדש. רבי ירמיה reports that רבי יוחנן does NOT apply ביטול מקח to הקדש. So the first version, where רבי יוחנן requires paying the difference only מדרבנן, fits him perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not reverse (don't switch who said which opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: Only רבי יונה's version needed the switch. In רבי ירמיה's version the names stay as they were, so the challenge from step 4 is gone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Do not reverse.
phrases.notes: He means: don't switch the opinions of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. Keep them as first quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4 by removing the need for the switch in רבי ירמיה's version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each version of רבי יוחנן's view gets its own attribution: no switch for רבי ירמיה, a switch only for רבי יונה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Switching the names would make רבי יוחנן contradict himself in רבי ירמיה's version.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי ירמיה, keep the original names, and everything fits.

steps.title: Do They Argue About שמואל's Rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יונה and רבי ירמיה disagree about whether to follow שמואל, who says הקדש worth a מנה can be redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about שמואל's ruling? שמואל said: הקדש worth a מנה that someone redeemed onto something worth a פרוטה is redeemed. So maybe רבי יונה does not accept שמואל's ruling, and רבי ירמיה does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to find the root of the argument between רבי יונה and רבי ירמיה. It suggests they disagree about שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says that redeeming הקדש for far less than it is worth still works. That means there is no ביטול מקח for הקדש. So the suggestion is: רבי ירמיה, who says no ביטול מקח for הקדש, agrees with שמואל, while רבי יונה, who says there is ביטול מקח for הקדש, disagrees with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Property set aside for the בית המקדש
A large sum (100 זוז)
Redeeming: moving the קדושה off an item onto money
The smallest coin value
He does not hold / he does hold (of a certain opinion)

phrases.english: Shall we say that they argue about Shmuel's ruling?
For Shmuel said:
Consecrated property worth a maneh
that one redeemed onto something worth a peruta
is redeemed.
That Rabbi Yona does not hold of Shmuel's ruling,
and Rabbi Yirmeya does hold of Shmuel's ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the two versions (רבי יונה and רבי ירמיה) are clear, the גמרא looks for what they really disagree about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the root of the disagreement between רבי יונה and רבי ירמיה about רבי יוחנן's view?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The suggestion: they argue about whether to follow שמואל's rule on redeeming הקדש for a פרוטה.

steps.title: Both Accept שמואל; They Argue About Doing It in the First Place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Both accept שמואל. רבי יונה holds שמואל meant only after the fact (דיעבד), while רבי ירמיה holds it is allowed even from the start (לכתחילה).
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both this one and that one accept שמואל's ruling. רבי יונה holds: when שמואל said it, he meant after it was already done, but he did not say it is allowed in the first place. רבי ירמיה holds: it is allowed even in the first place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says no, they don't argue about whether to accept שמואל. They only argue about how far שמואל's rule goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that, once done, redeeming הקדש for a פרוטה works. רבי יונה says you should not do this לכתחילה, which leaves room for his view that ביטול מקח applies to הקדש. רבי ירמיה says even לכתחילה it is fine, which fits his view that there is no ביטול מקח for הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this master and that master
After the fact, once it was already done
In the first place, as a plan from the start

phrases.english: No. Both this master and that master
hold of Shmuel's ruling.
For Rabbi Yona holds:
When Shmuel said it, it was about after the fact,
but he did not say it for doing it in the first place.
And Rabbi Yirmeya holds:
Even in the first place.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, בֵּין דְּמָר וּבֵין דְּמָר — אִית לֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 6 and moves the argument to דיעבד versus לכתחילה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי יונה disagrees with שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the only choices were accepting or rejecting שמואל. Really, both accept him and argue only about לכתחילה.

steps.title: Another Answer: Keep the Names and Explain the משנה Like רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a different answer: never switch the names, and solve the problem from the משנה of אלו דברים by explaining it the way רב חסדא does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really, do not reverse. And the משנה that was difficult for you, 'These are the matters... הקדשות', is explained like רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way out of the original problem. It keeps the names as first quoted in every version and deals with the challenging משנה a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא goes back to the earlier idea that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about a gap of exactly one-sixth, with ריש לקיש saying the difference is owed by Torah law. That idea had been dropped because the משנה of אלו דברים says הקדשות have no אונאה, which sounded like paying the difference is only rabbinic. If that משנה is read like רב חסדא, the problem disappears, so there is no need to move to ביטול מקח or to switch the names.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another answer
Our משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Two ways to handle the problem: (1) switch the names, but only in רבי יונה's version; or (2) never switch, and explain the משנה of אלו דברים like רב חסדא.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
Really, do not reverse.
And the mishna that was difficult for you,
'These are the matters... consecrated property',
is explained like Rav Chisda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the answer in step 2. Instead of moving to ביטול מקח and switching names, it keeps the argument on a one-sixth gap and removes the משנה's difficulty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה differently (following רב חסדא) instead of changing who said what.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה of אלו דברים (הקדשות have no אונאה) seemed to show that ריש לקיש could not hold that a one-sixth gap is owed to הקדש by Torah law. That pushed the argument to ביטול מקח, which in turn needed the switch of names.
steps.terutzMaskana: Keep the original names. They argue about a one-sixth gap, and the משנה, read like רב חסדא, does not contradict ריש לקיש's Torah-law view.

steps.title: רב חסדא's reading: holy property is never stuck with a mistaken price
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'אין להן אונאה' means הקדש is outside the normal overcharging rules. Even a mistake smaller than one sixth reverses the deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said: 'They have no אונאה' means they are not under the normal rules of אונאה, because even if the mistake is less than the usual amount, the deal is reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is filling in the answer from step 8 by quoting רב חסדא's explanation of the משנה in אלו דברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a price mistake under one sixth stays final. רב חסדא reads 'אין להן אונאה' as stricter, not more lenient: for these items, even a mistake below that limit is undone. Read this way, the משנה no longer suggests that paying the difference to הקדש is only rabbinic, so ריש לקיש can hold it is owed by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Under the normal system of overcharging rules
Less than the amount that normally counts as overcharging (less than one sixth)
Goes back; the deal is reversed or the difference is returned

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין להן אונאה' sounds like 'no overcharging rules, so anything goes.' רב חסדא reads it the opposite way: הקדש is so protected that even a small mistake is undone.

phrases.english: As Rav Chisda said:
"They have no overcharging rules"
means they are not under the normal rules of overcharging,
for even if it is less than the overcharging amount, the deal goes back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the content of the רב חסדא reading that step 8 pointed to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אין להן אונאה' means הקדש is lenient, so price mistakes are ignored.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means הקדש is stricter: even a mistake below one sixth reverses the deal.

steps.title: עולא: an appraisal by three cannot be reopened
steps.stepSummary: עולא limits the rule. A later higher appraisal only counts if the first appraisal was done by just two people. If three appraised it, even a hundred later appraisers cannot change it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: They only said this when it was appraised by two. But if it was appraised by three, even if a hundred people later come with a higher value, it does not go back.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא makes a new ruling: an appraisal of הקדש done properly by three people is final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Appraising הקדש requires three people. If only two appraised it, the appraisal was never proper, so a later higher value can override it. Once three appraised it properly, עולא treats the result as final, no matter how many later disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Appraised; its value was set
By two people
By three people (the proper number for appraising הקדש)
It does not go back; the deal stands

phrases.english: Ulla said:
They only said this when it was appraised by two,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule that a later, higher appraisal makes the buyer pay the difference to הקדש.

phrases.english: but when it was appraised by three,
even if a hundred people come afterward
it does not go back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: when exactly a mistaken appraisal of הקדש can be corrected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An appraisal of הקדש by three is final, even against a hundred later appraisers. Only an appraisal by two can be overridden.

steps.title: Challenge from רב ספרא: for appraisals we follow the majority
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא taught that 'a hundred are like two' applies only to witnesses. For appraisals we follow the majority of opinions, so the hundred should win against עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב ספרא said: Where do we say a hundred are like two and two are like a hundred? Only for testimony. For appraisals, we follow the number of opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא using a teaching of רב ספרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With witnesses, two count as fully as a hundred. רב ספרא says that equality does not apply to estimating value, where more opinions carry more weight. If so, a hundred later appraisers should outweigh the first three, which contradicts עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a word that opens a challenge)
A hundred are like two; more witnesses add no extra weight
Testimony by witnesses
An estimate or appraisal of value
We follow the number of opinions (the majority)

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Rav Safra say:
Where do we say that a hundred are like two
and two are like a hundred?
Regarding testimony,
but regarding estimating value
we follow the number of opinions.

steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that three appraisers cannot be overridden even by a hundred.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ספרא says appraisals follow the majority of opinions, so a hundred should outweigh three.

steps.title: Second challenge: even three against three should favor holy property
steps.stepSummary: Even if only three later appraisers disagree with the first three, we should follow the later, higher value, because הקדש always has the upper hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, with three against three, don't we follow the later ones? For הקדש always has the upper hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, even stronger challenge to עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first challenge needed a large majority. This one needs no majority at all: with three against three, the higher value should win. The reason is the principle that הקדש always gets the better side. That makes עולא's ruling even harder to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; introduces an additional challenge
The later one (here, the later appraisal)
הקדש has the upper hand; doubts are decided in favor of holy property

steps.whatToRemember: עולא says an appraisal by three is final. The גמרא pushes back twice: appraisals follow the majority (רב ספרא), and even three against three should favor הקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle יד הקדש על העליונה shows that הקדש gets extra protection in money matters. That is why עולא's finality rule needs a strong explanation.

phrases.english: And furthermore, with three against three,
don't we follow the later ones?
For holy property always has the upper hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger challenge to עולא on top of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that a first appraisal by three is final.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even without a majority, a later higher appraisal by an equal three should win, because הקדש always has the upper hand.

steps.title: עולא holds the appraisal rule is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenges to עולא. He holds that appraising and paying the value is only a rabbinic requirement, and the רבנן were lenient with their own rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא holds that the need to appraise the value comes from the words of the Sages, and with every rabbinic rule, the Sages were lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why עולא ignores the hundred later appraisers. The whole appraisal rule is only rabbinic, so the רבנן did not make it strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11 and 12 argued that a majority should win, or that הקדש should always get the higher value. The answer is that those strict ideas would apply to a Torah law. Since the appraisal is only מדרבנן, once three people have appraised, it is enough, and no one needs to pay more.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this is his view)
To make an appraisal (set the value)
From their words, meaning a rabbinic rule
They were lenient

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's limit (three appraisers are final) stands because the appraisal itself is a rabbinic rule, and the רבנן were lenient with it.

phrases.english: Ulla holds:
the need to make an appraisal is from their words (rabbinic),
and with anything rabbinic, the Rabbis were lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 11 and 12 against עולא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the source of the law (rabbinic, not Torah), which explains the leniency.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Majority rule, or the idea that הקדש always has the upper hand, should force following the later, higher appraisal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because appraising is only מדרבנן, the רבנן were lenient. A valid appraisal by three is final.

steps.title: משנה: 'in place of' an offering works only for a specific one
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. Saying 'this is in place of a burnt offering' with no specific offering means nothing. If he names a specific offering he has, or one at home, his words take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone said, 'This is in place of a burnt offering' or 'in place of a sin offering,' he has said nothing. If he said, 'in place of this sin offering' or 'in place of this burnt offering,' or 'in place of a sin offering or burnt offering that I have at home,' and he really had one, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that 'in place of' (תחת) works as a תמורה only when it points to a specific, existing offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תחת means swapping, which is תמורה. A swap needs something real to swap with. A general 'in place of an עולה' points to nothing, but 'this עולה' or 'the עולה I have at home' points to a real animal.

keyTerms.meaning: In place of; the language of exchanging (תְּמוּרָה)
He said nothing; his words have no effect
His words stand; they take effect

phrases.english: Mishnah:
"This is hereby in place of a burnt offering,"
phrases.notes: He is talking about his ordinary, non-holy animal.

phrases.english: or "in place of a sin offering"
he has said nothing.
"In place of this sin offering," or "in place of this burnt offering,"
or "in place of a sin offering" or "in place of a burnt offering
that I have in the house"
if he had one, his words stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the appraisal discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'In place of' takes effect only when it refers to a specific offering that really exists. A general reference does nothing.

steps.title: משנה: 'a burnt offering' versus 'for a burnt offering' with an unfit animal
steps.stepSummary: Saying an unfit animal 'is a burnt offering' does nothing. Saying it is 'for a burnt offering' means it is sold and the money buys a burnt offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said about a non-kosher animal or a blemished animal, 'These are a burnt offering,' he has said nothing. If he said, 'These are for a burnt offering,' they are sold, and with their money he brings a burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with animals that can never be offered. Everything depends on one small word: 'עולה' versus 'לעולה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unfit animal can never itself become an עולה, so 'these are an עולה' is impossible and means nothing. 'For an עולה' can mean 'for the purpose of an עולה', so it gives the animal monetary holiness. Then it is sold to buy a real עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher animal
An animal with a blemish, unfit for the altar
For a burnt offering (for its purpose)
With their money (the sale price)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't miss the tiny difference: 'עולה' (it IS an offering) does nothing, but 'לעולה' (FOR an offering) works through its value.

phrases.english: If he said about a non-kosher animal
or about a blemished animal
"These are hereby a burnt offering," he has said nothing.
If he said "These are hereby for a burnt offering,"
they are sold, and he brings a burnt offering with their money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עַל הַבְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה וְעַל בַּעֲלַת מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new case about animals unfit for the altar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calling an unfit animal 'an עולה' does nothing. Calling it 'for an עולה' means it is sold and the money buys an עולה.

steps.title: רב: the משנה does not follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב says the first ruling of the משנה cannot follow רבי מאיר. He holds that a person does not say words for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Our משנה is not like רבי מאיר. If it were like רבי מאיר, doesn't he hold that a person does not say his words for nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה. רב says the ruling 'he has said nothing' cannot fit רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that we always try to find some meaning in what a person says. So 'in place of an עולה' would be read as meaning an עולה he has at home, and it would take effect. Since the משנה says it means nothing, it must follow the Sages who disagree with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in accordance with (someone's view)
A person does not say his words for nothing

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next discussion of the גמרא. It shows how a general principle about how people speak can decide whether a statement about an offering takes effect.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Our Mishnah is not like Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: He means the first ruling, where 'in place of a burnt offering' does nothing.

phrases.english: for if it were like Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין אָדָם מוֹצִיא דְּבָרָיו לְבַטָּלָה.
phrases.english: doesn't he hold that a person does not say his words for nothing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first comment on the new משנה. It identifies whose opinion the first ruling follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling 'he has said nothing' does not follow רבי מאיר, who would find meaning in the words (an עולה at home).

steps.title: Inference: only completely unfit animals can be sold without a blemish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that unfit animals set aside 'for a burnt offering' are sold. It infers that this is only because they are totally unfit. A female set aside for an אשם or עולה would need a מום before being sold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'These are for a burnt offering' means they are sold, and he buys a burnt offering with the money. The reason they can be sold right away is that they are a non-kosher animal and a blemished animal, which are not fit for any offering, so they don't need a blemish. But if someone sets aside a female for an אשם or a עולה, it does need a blemish before it can be sold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats a line from the משנה in order to learn something from how it is worded. It is also setting up the next step, where רב says who this משנה cannot follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-kosher or blemished animal can never be brought on the מזבח, so only its money is holy, and it can be sold immediately. A female is not allowed as an אשם or a עולה, but it can be used for other קרבנות. So it has some holiness in its own body, and it must wait until it gets a מום before it can be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason, used to draw a precise inference from a ruling
They are not fit (to be offered)
One who sets aside a female animal
Guilt offering, which may only come from a male

steps.confusionAlert: The female is not completely unfit. It is just the wrong animal for this specific קרבן. That is exactly why it is treated differently from a non-kosher or blemished animal.

phrases.english: "These are hereby for a burnt offering"
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 15, about a non-kosher or blemished animal.

phrases.english: they are sold, and he brings a burnt offering with their money.
The reason is that they are a non-kosher animal and a blemished animal,
which are not fit to be offered,
so they do not need a blemish before being sold;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַפְרִישׁ נְקֵבָה לְאָשָׁם אוֹ לְעוֹלָה —
phrases.english: but one who sets aside a female for a guilt offering or for a burnt offering,
they do need a blemish.
phrases.notes: The female could still be used for a different קרבן, so it can't be sold until it gets a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה ruling from step 15 and draws an inference from its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only animals that are fully unfit may be sold without a מום. A female set aside for an אשם or עולה needs a מום first.

steps.title: רב: The משנה does not follow רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: given the inference just made, the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון rules that a female set aside for an אשם is sold without a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: our משנה is not like רבי שמעון. We learned that רבי שמעון says such a female may be sold without a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב uses the inference from the last step to identify which תנא the משנה does not follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that a female set aside for an אשם needs a מום before it can be sold. רבי שמעון treats such a female like a blemished animal, so only its money is holy and it can be sold right away. These two views clash, so the משנה cannot be רבי שמעון's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow (a certain תנא)
It is sold without a blemish

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a small inference from a משנה's wording can tell us which תנא the משנה follows.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
as we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Shimon says:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on 19b, about a female set aside for an אשם.

phrases.english: It is sold without a blemish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר רַב: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the inference of step 17 to show which תנא the משנה does not follow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה does not follow רבי שמעון, who allows a female set aside for an אשם to be sold without a מום.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה needs a מום for a female set aside for the wrong קרבן. רבי שמעון does not, so the משנה is not like רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing כיצד מערימין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the פרק כיצד מערימין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק כיצד מערימין.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק is finished, and the traditional closing line is said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is a formula said when finishing a פרק. It shows that we hope to come back and learn it again. No new הלכה is taught here.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
'How do we use a legal strategy', the name of this פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "How do we use a legal strategy."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after רב's final statement.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק כיצד מערימין is complete.
